11K likes, 219 comments - chrisburkard on October 16, 2026: "The final 2 days of Fatbiking & Packrafting the Oregon Coast Trail looked at the ground we’d covered & said “You ain’t seen nothing yet.” We had many good times, but a lot of hard going too. Hours on hours of riding through cold wet fog. The unrepentant moisture. High tides shutting down access points & forcing long reroutes. Logs, soft sand, and other obstacles making us carry our fully loaded bikes. The first 3/4 of the trip had tested us & we were feeling it. 

On day 7 though, something shifted. Fog & clouds lifted as we climbed Cape Blanco, revealing rugged headlands & wide sandy beaches soaring into the horizon. Traversing through those southern beaches, towns & capes was even better than it had appeared from above. We enjoyed sun for miles on end, and then, right around the end of day 7 as we approached the pistol river, the magic happened. Wind strummed the sand into gentle flows across the beach. The sun hummed lower, rapidly turning bright gold along the horizon. The waves seemed to crash on cue, their rich blue accentuating the intensity of the light. As we approached the next stacks of rocks, we saw it all come together in a symphony of light & movement played out across the jagged stage of rocks. It was a moment I’ll never forget. We all rode around in awe, soaking it all in, grateful to have gotten a perfect Oregon Coast evening at last. 

The high stuck with us after the sun set, but we had a few miles to go. We all locked back in after Kurt nearly got swept away by the Pistol River & gratefully slid into bed at Crook Point. 

Finally, the following day we entered the Samuel H Boardman scenic corridor. With only a few miles left to the border and plenty of time left in the day, we enjoyed the numerous stunning vistas on offer. We paddled across the Chetco River, the final crossing on our journey, and without any further fuss for the cyclists, we rode a few more miles of beach & road, the rolled up to the border of California. 

400 miles. 10 rivers paddled. Some very sandy smiles. We were done, and damn was that a good time.
@traveloregon @thepeoplescoast @oregonswildriverscoast @astraldesigns 

📸: @masoncasey @shredskyy".

1,313 likes, 5 comments - rapha_n_america on October 7, 2026: "Join Rapha ambassador @chrisburkard at the @oztrailsbikepark next Thursday, October 15 for afternoon laps and an evening screening of his latest film followed by a Q&A and signing.

An expedition 30 years in the making, “Searching for supercrust” explores the past, present, and future of Europe’s largest glacier through the stories of those who have braved the glacier’s icy expanse on two wheels.

Ticket sales, discounted lift passes and more info can be found at the link in our bio.".

posts.meta_description: 665 likes, 9 comments - chrisburkard on September 24, 2026: "The internet is ruthless when it comes to flubbing a scene in any image or video. They WILL notice, and they WILL call it out. It’s embarrassing for the photographer, the crew, and any brands involved. Generally speaking, it can be a death knell for a campaign or even an entire brand. Fortunately, there are easy ways to make sure that what your shooting is set up for success and building your scene properly is the biggest one. I touch on some of my thought process and considerations when it comes to scene building in photography in my latest and final episode of “Inside ‘Out There’” with my friends @sonyalpha. You can now view the full 6 part series on YouTube. Enjoy.".

posts.meta_description: 4,256 likes, 49 comments - chrisburkard on October 26, 2026: "We got totally fogged out deep in Iceland's Westfjords during a sailing photography workshop. Land was barely visible and, without even a breath of wind coming through, hopes for clear sky were far off. The only thing left to do was pull out the SUP, paddle across the eerily still water, and capture this surreal moment of stillness.".

13K likes, 225 comments - chrisburkard on October 14, 2026: "Sun rays blasted through the tall Sitka spruce & shore pine in Florence Oregon as we loaded our rafts to kick off day five of the Oregon Coast Trail. We were joined by heaps of seals as we paddled the Siuslaw River toward the south jetty & Oregon Dunes. The beauty of this crossing shot morale through the roof. The Oregon Dunes OHV area is capped by the Siuslaw on the north and the Umpqua on the south, forming an almost whale tail-esque geography, which meant we didn’t see town or road for two river crossings. 

For the Umpqua, we got lucky with a hiker/ biker ferry. We restocked food in Winchester Bay & continued south, into the fog, on a long stretch of isolated beach that would spit us out at the mouth of the Coos River & the massive Coo’s Bay. We paddled once again before rolling into Sunset Bay State Park at dusk & made camp in the beautiful yurts, that are housed at the campground there.

The morning featured a carb load at a local cafe & resupply since racoons got into some of our food overnight. Then, we pinned it south to Bandon! With a gusty paddle across the Coquille River, we landed in the sunny, busy town of downtown Bandon, grabbed great coffee & lunch and road south with the wind at our backs through the Lord of the Rings like sea stacks on the Bandon Beach. It was another beautiful moment on par with the sun rays from the morning prior, though a whole lot more moody with the fog rolling back in. 20 miles south through dropping temps and worsening fog, we reached Floras Lake and decided to call it a day. The soft sand was relentless on this stretch & we were starting to feel the wear and tear on our bikes and bodies. With two days to go, we were feeling good about our mileage and looked forward to the morning ride through Cape Blanco instead of doing it in the fog & dark.

@traveloregon @thepeoplescoast 

📸 by @masoncasey & @shredskyy".

8,943 likes, 63 comments - chrisburkard on October 12, 2026: "I'm offering a 1 day workshop in Laguna Beach this Sunday, October 18th. Field workshops are great, but I run classroom-based occasionally workshops because it allows me to engage more thoroughly with both subject-matter and you all who come to learn. I'll be going over some of the most important lessons I've taken away from my years as a professional photographer - everything from building a brand to best practices and working with clients, as well as shooting and photo-theory. Spots are filling up so be sure to grab your place now!

This workshop caps off an incredible weekend with @coastfilmfestival where I’ll be screening my film “Searching For SuperCrust” and speaking alongside the likes of John John Florence and other incredible athletes and artists. You can find tickets and details for all their excellent events on their page".

5,079 likes, 93 comments - chrisburkard on October 11, 2026: "Day 4 on the Oregon Coast Trail kicked off with a misty bridge crossing in dense fog as we crossed the Yaquina River departing Newport. This was one of the only bridges on our route due to the long jetty rocks and lack safe beach exits for our rafts. For the next 50 miles we reveled in relatively pleasant weather and good riding too. We paddled across the Alsea Bay with fairly calm water. The whole crew then stopped at an epic little bike co-op in Waldport to rinse the sand and salt corroded gear before continuing down the beach to the volcanic reefs above Yachats. In town, we stopped at one of the best coffee shops on the whole trip and soaked in some sun and the view south before continuing on till nightfall. 

We crashed for the night at a campsite near Florence OR, marking the 200 mile point of our journey from Astoria to Brookings…. almost the exact midpoint. Spirits were still high even though the legs felt heavy. Still a lot of coast left to go.
@newportoregon @visit.yachats 

📸: @masoncasey @shredskyy".

4,547 likes, 38 comments - chrisburkard on October 11, 2026: "I’m screening my latest film “Searching For SuperCrust” in Bentonville Arkansas this Thursday October 15th! I’ll be riding OZ Trails Bikepark and then hosting a great evening there.  I’ll present the film, give a bit of behind the scenes and time for Q&A then be around to mingle and sign books and prints. Some tickets are still available so grab them now! You can go to searchingforsupercrust.com or just click the link on my page. 

This is a collection of a few more intimate and striking frames from the film. As we traversed Vatnajokull not everything was captured as stills, so these only were revealed as we started going through the footage itself.".

posts.meta_description: 13K likes, 149 comments - chrisburkard on October 10, 2026: "Day 3 of Fat biking & Pack rafting down the Oregon Coast Trail started in a thick fog with some hard high-tide pedaling. Crossing the Nestucca was choppy and pretty intense with the wind and being unable to see the other side. But after the first river crossing the tide began to retreat revealing nice firm sand for riding and a hint of sun through the clouds. By the time we reached Lincoln City it was bright and beautiful. We got a whole lot of excited questions and curious looks from the fisherman when we started blowing up our rafts and prepping to paddle the Siletz River. The fog returned later in the day but was a lot spottier and getting some rad riding through the woods made up for it. We ended the day warming up with fish, chips, and chowder at Mo’s in Lincoln City which felt very appropriate for another excellent day on the Oregon Coast. ~150 miles down and 219 to go!".

8,609 likes, 90 comments - chrisburkard on October 5, 2026: "Arguably the best show on earth, and it's not even on earth.
Shot in Death Valley's Mesquite Dunes on assignment for @natgeo in 2023 for their 'Ultimate Guide to the National Parks'. My team toured 3 national parks to capture them in all their beauty - park 3/3 was Death Valley.

This image and others are available as prints, in any size and style you can imagine, on my store. Order now to get ahead on your holiday gifts!

Shot on @sonyalpha A7RV
Lens: 14mm
ISO: 3200
Aperture: f1.8
Shutter: 25s".
